Facts: A public official (尹某) who is a director-level staff in land resources bureau, used his position to accept bribes (cash, shopping cards, etc.) from a company representative in exchange for favorable treatment in land project bidding and contracting. This is classic "受贿" (accepting bribes) or "滥用职权"? Actually "受贿" is the charge for public officials accepting bribes. The lexicon includes "受贿" and also "滥用职权". The facts show he accepted bribes, not necessarily abusing power beyond that. The charge "受贿" is appropriate.

Also there is "对非国家工作人员行贿" (bribing non-state staff) but not relevant.

Thus the charge is "受贿". Possibly also "滥用职权" if he abused his authority to give preferential treatment. However the typical charge for a public official who accepts bribes is "受贿". The lexicon also includes "非国家工作人员受贿" (bribery by non-state staff) but not relevant.

Thus answer: [罪名]受贿<eoa>

Check if any other charges: "非法占有" not listed. "贪污" not listed. So just "受贿".

Thus final.
